references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew 27:54 tells us that the officer and those who were guarding Jesus said, 'Truly this was God's Son!' Mark has a similar confession in Mark 15:39. Luke uses the word 'righteous' (δίκαιος) instead of 'God's Son', which emphasizes Jesus' innocence.

Pilate declared that he found no guilt in Jesus (Luke 23:4). The officer's words stating that Jesus was a righteous man confirm this declaration of innocence and form a framework around the passion narrative in Luke.
Pilate repeated that he found no guilt in Jesus (Luke 23:14-15). The officer's recognition at the cross—that this man truly was righteous—provides the final confirmation of what Pilate had said.

The thief on the cross confessed that Jesus had done nothing wrong (Luke 23:41). The officer's words are the third testimony in Luke's passion narrative regarding Jesus' innocence, following Pilate and the thief.

Isaiah prophesied about the suffering servant: 'My righteous servant' (Isaiah 53:11). The officer's confession that Jesus was 'righteous' (δίκαιος) points back to this prophecy concerning the Messiah as the righteous one.
Peter calls Jesus 'the Holy and Righteous One' in Acts 3:14. The officer's words at the cross anticipate this apostolic confession of Jesus' righteousness.

Stephen calls Jesus 'the Righteous One' (Acts 7:52). Luke uses this title repeatedly in his two-volume work, and the officer's statement at the cross serves as an important foundation for this Christological title.

Ananias tells Paul that God has chosen him to see 'the Righteous One' (Acts 22:14). The title 'the Righteous One' runs like a red thread through Luke-Acts, with the officer's confession serving as a central testimony.

John calls Jesus 'Jesus Christ, the Righteous One' (1 John 2:1). The officer's recognition of Jesus' righteousness at the cross is an early testimony that aligns with the broader New Testament understanding of Jesus as the righteous one.

Psalm 22 concludes with a vision that God's righteousness will be proclaimed to future generations (Psalm 22:32). The officer's glorification of God and recognition of Jesus' righteousness at the cross is a fulfillment of this prophetic vision that God's saving work will be testified to.
